slides.say: In how many different ways can seven different trophies be placed in a row in a glass cabinet?
So we put seven different items in a row. Like in the lesson, a row is a choice without repetition.
at: So we put seven different items

slides.say: Let's solve it the math way, in stages. Seven trophies and seven places in the row, so seven stages.
The first place can take any of the seven trophies. Seven options.
That trophy is placed, so it's out. The second place has six left.
Then five, four, three and two.
at: Then five, four, three and two

slides.say: And the last place has only one trophy left. No choice at all.
at: the last place has only one

slides.say: Now we multiply, one step at a time. Seven times six is forty-two.
Forty-two times five is two hundred ten.
Two hundred ten times four is eight hundred forty.
Eight hundred forty times three is two thousand five hundred twenty.
And times two is five thousand forty. Times one doesn't change it.
at: And times two is five thousand forty

slides.say: That's seven factorial. Seven different items in a row, seven factorial ways.
A lot of students write seven times seven, forty-nine. That's choice number four. But a trophy can't stand in two places, so the pool shrinks.
Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
